did_you_know.text: The psalm opens with the heading “A Song of Ascents. Of David,” identifying it as a song belonging to the genre of the Songs of Ascents.
The verse describes brothers living together with two complementary words—“good” and “pleasant”—emphasizing both the value of unity and its positive feeling.
The expression “when brothers live together in unity” places the very experience of brothers living together at the center of the psalm’s message.
Unity is compared to precious oil flowing down on Aaron’s head, down Aaron’s beard and to the edge of his garments—a description that emphasizes abundance and spreading.
Aaron is mentioned by name, so the image also connects the oil with the priestly figure and his ceremonial clothing.
In the second verse, the verb “flows down” is repeated twice: the oil flows down onto the head and then onto the beard, creating a sense of continuous movement from top to bottom.
The dew falling from Mount Hermon onto the mountains of Zion is an image of freshness and abundance, continuing the idea of downward movement from the previous verse.
The psalm’s conclusion links Zion with divine blessing: “For there the LORD has commanded the blessing,” and the blessing is defined as “life forevermore.”
